title: Return: free will, then a job offer, then back to free will
description: Two friends argue about free will and determinism, switch to Marcus's job offer, then explicitly go back to free will. Expect three occurrences; the third is a new free-will node on the same thread as the first, with a revisit edge back to it.

utterances.text: I watched this lecture last night that totally broke my brain. The guy argued free will basically doesn't exist.
Sapolsky? He's been everywhere lately. The whole thing about how every choice is just biology plus environment.
Yeah! He says if you trace any decision back far enough, it's neurons, hormones, childhood, genes. There's no point where "you" step in.
I kind of buy it, honestly. Like, I didn't choose to be the kind of person who likes running. I just am.
But then nobody's responsible for anything. That feels wrong. Should we stop punishing people?
He'd say yes to punishment as revenge, no to keeping dangerous people away from others. More like quarantine than blame.
That's bleak. But also kind of compassionate? I can't decide.
Totally. Okay, wait, I have to tell you, I got the offer from the design agency.
No way! The one in Gastown? Congrats! Are you taking it?
I don't know yet. It's more money, like fifteen percent more, but I'd be leaving my team right before our big launch.
How do you feel about your manager though? You've been complaining about her for months.
That's the thing. She's the main reason to leave. The new place said I'd get a senior title too.
Then it sounds like you already know. Do they want an answer soon?
By Friday. I'm going to negotiate for one more week of vacation first.
Smart. Ask for the vacation in writing.
Okay but going back to the free will thing, I keep thinking about it. If it's all determined, was your job decision ever really yours?
Ha, that's exactly what I was thinking. Like, I'm going to "decide" by Friday, but my brain probably already knows.
Right, and if it's predetermined, then all my agonising over stuff is just theatre.
Unless the agonising is part of the cause. The deliberating still matters, it's just not magic.
Huh, that's compatibilism, right? Free will is just acting on your own reasons without being forced.
Yeah, Dennett's take. I think that's where I land. It's free enough to be worth wanting.
